text:
sam: Heads-up — I’m seeing a p99 spike on /chat/compose since the kernel-selector update rolled last night. Dashboard snapshot: https://console.redwood.ai/d/snap/abc123 (staging). Anyone oncall?

maya: Which selector? the auto-v2 change? We flipped policy to prefer attn-opt only for seq<=256, otherwise auto-v2.

observability-bot: alert: route=/chat/compose p99 increased from 380ms -> 920ms (1h window). Alert ID: #A-2026-0317-09

liam: I pulled a few traces. Token-level waterfall shows big tails at the final 30-60 tokens. KV cache hit-rate dips align with those tails. Also noticed batch_size pushed up for a subset of requests (batches of 20+). Paste: ```trace id: t-9f3a; kernel=auto-v2; batch_size=22; kv_hit_pct=62; tail_latency=750ms```

sam: That matches what I suspected — batching heuristics biased towards larger batches after the throughput tweak. Larger batches + cold KV misses = bad tail. We should treat /chat/compose as latency-sensitive and cap batch size. Propose: per-route override max_batch=8 and force kv_prefetch=true.

maya: Agreed we should expose per-route overrides in Console. UX: small card for routes should include p50/p95/p99, throughput (req/s), error rate, and kv_hit%. Clicking expands to token-level waterfall and recent traces. Thoughts?

anya: Ran a quick staging experiment: rolled back selector for /chat/compose to attn-opt for seq<=512 and capped batch to 8. Results (staging, 30m window): before rollback p99=980ms, p95=310ms, p50=78ms; after rollback p99=420ms, p95=210ms, p50=70ms. kv_hit_pct improved from 64% -> 85% on avg.

liam: We should also emit these fields on every trace: kernel_name, kernel_variant, batch_size, kv_hit_pct, chosen_by_policy. Right now we only tag kernel_name in some traces. That will let us attribute regressions quickly. Also add a histogram for batch_size in metrics ingestion.

sam: Agreed. Also need token-level latency buckets (per-token micro-latencies) so the waterfall chart in Console can be accurate without storing full traces for every request. Reservoir sampling of tokens on ingest should be fine.

maya: I can add the card prototype. UX question: show kv_hit% as a single number or micro-sparkline over the last hour? Suggest both: single aggregated number + sparkline for trend. Waterfall on click.

liam: One more instrumentation note — when kernels fall back to quantized variants, we see different tail shapes. We need a 'fallback_reason' tag (e.g., capacity, OOM, kernel_mismatch) so dashboards can filter fallback-induced tails.

observability-bot: deploy-bot: kernel-selector auto-v2 rollout: canary 10% -> started 2026-03-17T09:12Z.

sam: Action items summary: 1) eng-runtime: emit kernel_name/variant, batch_size histograms, kv_hit_pct per-inference + fallback_reason tag; 2) eng-platform/console: add per-route small card with p50/p95/p99, tps, error rate, kv_hit%, sparkline and expand-to-waterfall; 3) ops: add a per-route sampling job to run max_batch=8 experiment in prod canary for latency-sensitive routes.

maya: I'll open a Console PR with wireframe + ingestion fields required. Will also add a backlog ticket for expand-to-waterfall flow.

liam: I'll add telemetry PR to include batch_size and fallback_reason and a histogram metric for batch_size.

anya: I'll keep the rollback config in staging until we have telemetry and console cards to validate.

sam: Thanks — quick ask: can we get a short p99-by-kernel breakdown for the last 6h? That will help decide whether to pin a kernel per route or tune heuristics.

maya: Yeah — I'll add a quick ad-hoc dashboard and drop link later.

liam: noted, will prioritize telemetry change.

observability-bot: note: incident channel #inc-125 linked for postmortem if needed.

sam: Great thread. :thumbsup:
